title: AI’s Regimes of Representation: A Community-centered Study of Text-to-Image Models in South Asia

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative focus group study where participants from India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh co-designed culturally specific text prompts and evaluated Text-to-Image (T2I) model outputs for cultural recognition failures, hegemonic Western/North Indian defaults, and exoticizing tropes.

Community-based qualitative analysis of generated images for prompts relating to Muslim identity and Islamic locales, identifying one-dimensional stereotypes such as the over-representation of veils, prayer caps, and mosques.

Focus group reflections on T2I outputs generated from prompts specifying Dalit communities, assessing the perpetuation of disempowered, impoverished stereotypes and the erasure of Dalit cultural practices in favor of upper-caste defaults.

Evaluating generated images of South Asian daily life, cities, and indigenous (Adivasi) communities to identify the pervasive algorithmic reproduction of tropes related to poverty, slums, and underdevelopment.
